tldr: CoPaw added 4605 stars this week, the largest absolute gain, while Ouroboros grew 20.9% from a smaller base.
Hermes Agent crossed 224k stars and remains the most-starred multi-tenant project in the tracked set.
14 of 43 projects were flat or declining, so momentum is concentrating in a handful of runtimes.
Compiled runtimes average an 80 security score versus 69 for scripting runtimes, with better sandboxing and lower shell risk.
36 projects are local-first and 33 offer cloud-optional operation, leaving only 9 that require a cloud dependency.

sections.movement: Star movement this cycle was top-heavy. CoPaw and Hermes Agent together accounted for more than two-thirds of the 11,593 new stars across 43 projects, while 14 projects stayed flat or lost ground. The fastest percentage growers came from smaller bases: Ouroboros at 20.9% and CoPaw at 16.8% show that early-stage projects can still capture attention quickly. For a developer choosing a tool, the signal is that community energy is flowing toward a few established names and a handful of fast risers, not evenly across the ecosystem.
sections.security: The median security score across all 43 projects is 75, but the split between compiled and scripting runtimes reveals a practical gap. Compiled runtimes average 80 with stronger sandboxing and lower shell risk, while scripting runtimes average 69 with a median shell risk of 7. Ten projects still allow unsupervised shell access, which is a concrete risk for any deployment that touches untrusted input. Hardened projects number only 12, so a developer who needs runtime isolation should verify sandboxing and shell posture directly rather than relying on the ecosystem median.
sections.posture: Local-first operation is the norm: 36 projects support it, and 33 of those also offer cloud-optional paths. Only 9 projects require a cloud connection, which limits offline use and introduces a dependency on a third-party service. Licensing is dominated by MIT at 20 projects and Apache-2.0 at 10, with only 3 copyleft-licensed projects. Ten projects have no clear license, which is a practical blocker for commercial integration. A developer who needs full offline operation and predictable licensing has plenty of options, but should verify both before committing.
